title: Delete or rewrite the 474 row-existence-only Drift Manager-API tests in test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart — none can detect an ordering or filtering regression
rule: TQ-8 (tautological tests / assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong) + Feathers lens (test has no seam to the behavior it claims to cover)
area: test/core/database (Drift generated Manager API coverage tests)

evidence.quote:
/// OrderBy + filter coverage for all remaining uncovered ColumnOrderings and
/// ColumnFilters getters in user_database.g.dart.
// createdAt defaults to currentDateAndTime; just verify the filter compiles and executes

/// Additional coverage for annotation composer getters that were missed in
/// the first computed fields test — focuses on fields like id, profileId,

/// Coverage for annotation composer ($$XxxAnnotationComposer) getters
/// in user_database.g.dart.

why: Every one of these 474 tests inserts exactly one row in setUp, then calls orderBy/filter/computedField/withFields and asserts only `hasLength(1)`/`isNotEmpty`/`isA<List<...>>`. Confirmed by exhaustive grep: zero occurrences anywhere in the 2435-line orderby file of `hasLength(0)`, `hasLength(2)`, or `equals([...])` — no test ever inserts a second, differently-ordered or non-matching row, so a broken `.asc()`/`.desc()` (or a filter predicate that matches everything, or one that silently no-ops) still returns the single seeded row and the test stays green. Ran both the smallest (crossref_filter_test.dart) and largest (orderby_test.dart) files in this session: 26/26 and 283/283 pass today, so this is 474 currently-green CI checkmarks that give zero regression protection for the very ordering/filtering behavior their names promise. Compounding it: `grep -rl '\.managers\.' lib/` returns 0 files — the Drift-generated Manager API under test (`db.managers.*`) has no caller anywhere in production code; the app queries through hand-written DAOs instead. This is ~5900 lines of test code (this batch alone) written to drive `flutter test --coverage` numbers up against a generated-code surface the app never exercises, at real cost: CI/build time on every run, and reviewer/agent attention budget on every future change to user_database.dart (per AG-3's own rationale about per-file read budgets).
recommendation: Delete this suite — `db.managers.*` has no production caller, so there is no behavior left to protect. If the underlying goal was raising `user_database.g.dart` line-coverage numbers, exclude generated files from the coverage gate instead (e.g. `lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info '*.g.dart' '*.freezed.dart'` in the coverage make target) rather than writing assertion-free tests. If any ordering/filtering behavior here genuinely needs protecting because a DAO wraps it, move that coverage to the DAO's own test file with real assertions: insert ≥2 rows with distinct sort keys and assert exact order via `equals([...])`, and insert ≥1 matching + ≥1 non-matching row per filter test and assert the non-matching row is excluded.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn 'db.managers' test/core/database/user_database_managers_*_test.dart` returns nothing (files deleted), OR every remaining orderBy test seeds ≥2 rows with distinct values and asserts exact order, and every remaining filter test seeds ≥1 excluded row and asserts it's excluded.
Coverage tooling (`make test` / CI) excludes `*.g.dart` and `*.freezed.dart` from the coverage report, removing the incentive that produced this suite.
`flutter test --coverage` line count for `test/core/database/` drops by roughly the amount removed, verifiable via `wc -l` before/after in the PR diff.
